children: is expected to rise 13.7% over the next 12 months, while the 10-year Treasury yield
is seen falling to 4.5% from 5% currently, according to Goldman Sachs.

The bank's 12-month target for the S&P 500 is 8,700, up from 7,651 currently. Goldman Sachs sees the index at 8,000 in three months and 8,300 in six months, implying gains of 4.6% and 8.5%, respectively.
The forecast also pointed to gains across other major equity markets. Goldman Sachs sees the STOXX Europe 600
at 695 in 12 months from 635 currently, representing a 9.4% increase.
The MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan index is projected to rise 27.2% to 1,120 from 880, while Japan's Topix is seen reaching 4,600 from 4,091, a 12.4% increase.

Goldman Sachs said it expects Treasury yields to decline over the same period. The US10Y is forecast at 4.8% in three months and 4.7% in six months before reaching 4.5% in 12 months, a 54-basis-point decline from the current 5% level.
Germany's 10-year yield is projected to fall to 3.3% from 3.5%, while Japan's 10-year yield is seen at 2.9% from 2.9% currently after reaching 3% in three and six months.

The bank's currency forecasts pointed to a stronger yen but weaker euro and pound against the dollar. The euro-dollar rate is projected at 1.12 in 12 months from 1.15 currently, while sterling is seen at $1.28 from $1.34. The dollar-yen rate is forecast at 165 from 157, implying a 5.2% increase.
Goldman Sachs also said it expects commodity prices to diverge. Gold

is forecasted at $5,140 an ounce in 12 months from $4,352 currently, an 18.1% increase. Brent crude is projected to fall to $78 a barrel from $103.9, while NYMEX natural gas is seen at $2.75 per MMBtu from $2.90. LME copper is forecast at $13,800 per metric ton, down from $14,543 currently.

title: Goldman bets on falling yields, rising stocks
